title: Gate extension benchmark/fetch commands on advertised capabilities
description: The client/fetch surface can issue STARTTLS, AUTHINFO, CHECK, TAKETHIS, POST, and IHAVE directly without first checking CAPABILITIES. That is useful for raw protocol probes, but an RFC-compliant benchmark client should not treat extension hot paths as benchmarkable unless the server advertises the relevant capability: RFC 3977 section 3.3 for capability discovery, RFC 4642 for STARTTLS, RFC 4643 for AUTHINFO, and RFC 4644 for STREAMING CHECK/TAKETHIS. Add a capability-aware benchmark mode or mark these one-shot commands as raw probes in CLI/docs so throughput results are not mistaken for negotiated client behavior.

title: Stored article_dir articles do not preserve selector state
description: RFC 3977 sections 6.2.1-6.2.4 require stored ARTICLES to set current article state correctly: numeric selectors should return 423 for a missing article number after GROUP, and successful numeric ARTICLE should update current article while message-id ARTICLE should not clobber it. Current article_dir-backed server returns 411/412 instead. Repro is covered by src/lib.rs::rfc3977_compliance_article_file_backend_preserves_selector_state_and_errors.

title: article_dir index build errors are silently ignored
description: src/lib.rs:3652-3656 converts ArticleStoreIndex::build(root) to Option with .ok(), so permission/read/parse-path errors silently disable indexed GROUP/LIST/OVER/HDR/NEWGROUPS/NEWNEWS behavior while article_dir remains configured. That makes benchmark server behavior depend on an unreported startup failure. Surface the error from ServerConfig construction or log/track it explicitly, and add a test for unreadable/bad article_dir setup.

title: Indexed OVER/HDR paths reread and reparse article files per row
description: src/lib.rs:5426-5456 selects article numbers from the in-memory index, but append_overview_row_for_entry and append_header_row_for_entry at 5513-5558 call fs::read and Article::parse for every row. Wide OVER/HDR ranges can re-read many files per request, which is a poor fit for a benchmark server. Consider caching parsed header metadata/body counts in ArticleStoreEntry during ArticleStoreIndex::build, or add a benchmark proving the current cost is acceptable for article_dir workloads.
close_reason: done

title: Make benchmark request generator group-aware for numeric selectors
description: client_request_for_command emits numeric ARTICLE/BODY requests for command_id values within MAX_ARTICLE_NUMBER when no segment file is provided. Numeric article selectors are only meaningful after selecting a group; RFC 3977 sections 6.2.1-6.2.4 scope article-number selectors to the currently selected group and servers correctly answer 412 before GROUP. A benchmark workload using these generated numeric requests without a GROUP warmup measures error paths rather than retrieval. Add a group-aware benchmark mode that sends GROUP/LISTGROUP setup before numeric-selector workloads, or prefer message-id selectors unless the workload explicitly manages selected-group state.
close_reason: done

title: Explicit CAPABILITIES marks negotiation complete before response succeeds
description: src/client.rs:1771-1778 and 1805-1811 call mark_capabilities_negotiated before the CAPABILITIES response is received or validated. If CAPABILITIES fails or returns an invalid frame while the connection remains usable enough for queued work, later extension commands can skip the required preflight. Mark negotiated only after a successful CAPABILITIES response, and add a test where the server rejects/malforms CAPABILITIES and a subsequent extension request must not proceed as negotiated.
close_reason: done

title: Capability negotiation holds a Mutex guard across network await
description: src/client.rs:1851-1858 locks capabilities_negotiated and then awaits queue_request_unchecked(...).receive(). Holding a tokio::Mutex guard across a network response is non-idiomatic and serializes all concurrent first extension requests behind I/O. Replace this with a OnceCell/OnceLock-style negotiation future or a small state machine so concurrent requests share the same CAPABILITIES result without holding the mutex while awaiting the server.
close_reason: done

title: README says client/fetch do not negotiate capabilities, but code now does
description: README.md:15-18 says client and fetch are raw probes that do not negotiate capabilities first. Current ClientConnection now sends CAPABILITIES before extension commands such as POST/IHAVE/CHECK/TAKETHIS/AUTHINFO/STARTTLS/OVER/HDR/NEWGROUPS/NEWNEWS, and tests assert that behavior. Update the docs and CLI help wording so benchmark users understand which requests are raw and which are capability-preflighted.

comments.author: mjc
comments.text:
# NNTP RFC Compliance Audit Matrix

This matrix records the current compliance evidence for the benchmark
client/server implementation. It is scoped to the NNTP RFCs currently exercised
by the codebase:

- RFC 3977, Network News Transfer Protocol
- RFC 4642, STARTTLS
- RFC 4643, AUTHINFO
- RFC 4644, STREAMING
- RFC 2980, selected legacy extensions

Status meanings:

- `covered`: current tests or implementation evidence directly cover the item.
- `partial`: current evidence covers part of the item but leaves meaningful gaps.
- `follow-up`: tracked outside this matrix by a Beads issue.
- `not in scope`: the current mock server/client intentionally does not implement
  the capability; tests should prove it is not advertised or is rejected with the
  correct response.

Current test inventory: `rg -n "fn rfc|async fn rfc" src` reports 94 RFC-named
tests, and `rg -n "rfc4642|rfc4643|rfc4644|rfc2980|rfc3977" src` reports 988 RFC
references in test and implementation comments.

## RFC 3977 Core

| Area | RFC sections | Current evidence | Status | Gaps / next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command line limits and CRLF termination | 3.1, 9.2, 9.8 | `src/protocol.rs` request-line parser tests; `src/lib.rs` server syntax tests; `src/terminator.rs` line terminator tests | covered | Renamed green RFC audit tests under `nntpbench-v4f`. |
| Command keyword grammar and argument counts | 3.1, 9.2 | `rfc3977_compliance_request_line_grammar_matrix`, server syntax matrices, request builder tests | covered | Keep coverage mapped when renaming tests. |
| Multiline command/data framing | 3.1.1 | `src/terminator.rs` multiline terminator tests; `src/lib.rs` TAKETHIS batch tests; article parser dot-stuffing tests | covered | Benchmark fixtures still need a separate valid-path audit under `nntpbench-hb5`. |
| Response framing and generic errors | 3.2, 3.2.1, 9.4 | `ResponseFraming::for_request_status` tests; `ResponseFrame::parse` status/shape tests | covered | The full server command-state cross-product is tracked by `nntpbench-3k5`. |

title: Add RFC session setup benchmarks beyond raw command roundtrips
description: The end-to-end benches mostly measure raw command roundtrips against the mock server: message-id ARTICLE/BODY, CAPABILITIES, DATE, and a mixed pipeline. They do not model full RFC reader sessions with greeting validation, CAPABILITIES discovery, optional MODE READER, GROUP selection, current article movement, LISTGROUP setup, and then article/overview/header commands over selected state. RFC 3977 sections 5, 6, 7, and 8 define those session flows. Add benchmark scenarios that include setup amortization and steady-state selected-group workloads so client/server performance claims cover compliant reader behavior as well as isolated command hot paths.
close_reason: completed

title: Normalize green RFC audit test names
description: The RFC audit tests were originally intentional failure probes. After making them green, normalize the test naming so the suite communicates passing compliance coverage. Preserve RFC references and grouping while reducing churn.
close_reason: Renamed green RFC audit tests to the rfc*_compliance_* naming scheme and moved audit matrix storage into Beads.

title: Derive overview/header responses from article_dir
description: When --article-dir is enabled, OVER, HDR, XOVER, and XHDR still return static fixture responses. That makes file-backed benchmark server responses inconsistent: ARTICLE can come from disk while overview and header views still describe synthetic fixture articles. RFC 3977 sections 8.3-8.6 and RFC 2980 cover these commands as views over server articles. Add tests that load stored articles with headers/dates/groups and require OVER/HDR/XOVER/XHDR to reflect that store, or clearly scope article_dir to ARTICLE-only payload benchmarking.
close_reason: completed

title: Derive file-backed HEAD/BODY/STAT from article_dir
description: The benchmark server's --article-dir path only affects ARTICLE. In src/lib.rs handle_command, RequestKind::Article calls write_stored_article_response(...), but HEAD, BODY, and STAT ignore config.article_dir and synthesize canned responses. RFC 3977 sections 6.2.1-6.2.4 define ARTICLE, HEAD, BODY, and STAT as article retrieval commands over the same selected article/message-id semantics; with --article-dir, benchmark runs for HEAD/BODY/STAT can measure synthetic data that disagrees with ARTICLE. Add stored-article tests for current, numeric, and message-id HEAD/BODY/STAT, then derive those frames from stored ARTICLE content or explicitly prevent --article-dir from being used for non-ARTICLE benchmarks.
close_reason: done
